newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks end year on upbeat note.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks end year on upbeat note.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks ended the year on a positive note after a volatile 12 months which saw the index fell to its lowest level in recent times, brokers said.
The all share closed 0.36 points up at 602.96. Turnover was 59.31 million rupees.
"The index closed firm because some locals are buying in anticipation of an improvement in the index in early January," said Shanil Perera, a broker at Lanka Securities.
The main trades were 75,000 Aitken Spcence & Co at 89.50 rupees, 200,000 Blue Diamonds Jewellery 10.25 rupees, and 60,000 Grain Elevators at 14 rupees.

A quantity of 50,000 Lanka Lubricants, which rose 10 rupees to 50, 15,000 National Development Bank at 195 rupees, 122,500 Sampath Bank at 46 rupees and 1.7 million Vanik at 15.50 rupees, were also sold.
The all share fell below 600 points for the first time in three years in late June, thanks to a severe drought from March to August which led to power cuts and poor corporate profits.
"Investors see prices rising with more trading, when foreign funds enter the market in the new year," said Perera.
The recently launched Centry Growth Fund is also expected to enter the market in early 1997.
